_comment: Hand-entered corrections for individual talks, applied last in the build
(see scripts/apply-talk-overrides.mjs). Use this whenever a talk's event,
title, date or location is wrong: the fetchers wipe their own directories
every build, so editing the generated YAML does not survive.
Key = the YouTube video id, the one identifier that survives a re-fetch.
Value = any of: title, event, event_url, session_url, date, end_date,
location, role, abstract, co_speakers (array), tags (array), featured.
Dates are the day the talk was GIVEN, never the day the video went up.
Overrides whose video id matches nothing are reported by the script, so a
typo or a delisted video does not fail silently.

r1gpPpNhT_4._why: Scrape read the video title as the channel name, so title and event were swapped.
r1gpPpNhT_4.title: Breaking Free with Open Standards: OpenTelemetry and Perses for Observability

XVEPKb0aCx8._why: CNCF's channel publishes from every KubeCon, so no matcher can claim this one safely. Confirmed by Kasper as KubeCon EU 2026.
XVEPKb0aCx8.title: Taming Complexity: Building Observable Workflows With Dapr and OpenTelemetry

Nlx8jSfe8UQ._why: Same as above. Given at Observability Day, the CNCF-hosted co-located event at KubeCon EU 2026, which is also what the photos from those days belong to.
Nlx8jSfe8UQ.title: Observability at the Edge: State of OpenTelemetry in Kubernetes Ingress Controllers

tSBfDzStoYE._why: CNCF's channel can't identify an event, so this keynote sat apart from the KubeCon EU 2025 engagement it belongs to. Confirmed by Kasper.
tSBfDzStoYE.title: Keynote: The Observability Platform Engineering Advantage: From Zero-Code to Monitoring as Code
